LESSON: SPEAKING FLUENCY: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1.1: Speaking Fluency: pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Speaking Fluency: pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to speak accurately and express the right feelings?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct sentences orally using words related to the theme
2. speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic
3. use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SPEAKING FLUENCY: PRONUNCIATION
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Speaking Fluency: pronunciation helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SPEAKING FLUENCY: PRONUNCIATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Construct sentences orally using words related to the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences orally using words related to the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences orally using words related to the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Speaking Fluency: pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences orally using words related to the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic

What this means
In this part you learn to speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Speaking Fluency: pronunciation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Speaking Fluency: pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Speaking Fluency: pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: construct sentences orally using words related to the theme)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Speaking Fluency: pronunciation to a partner. (skill: speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Speaking Fluency: pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct sentences orally using words related to the theme.
3. Practise this skill: speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic.
4. Practise this skill: use vocabulary related to the theme correctly in oral communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Speaking Fluency: pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Speaking Fluency: pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to speak accurately and express the right feelings?
2. How can you listen more attentively?
3. Which words do you use to talk about diseases?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Speaking Fluency: pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: construct sentences orally using words related to the theme.
5. Be able to: speak accurately, at the right speed and with expression on a given topic.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
